newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
THE CAPTAIN SLOCUM RACE

October 10 marks the centenary of the arrival in Sydney Harbour of one of the most famous sailors of all time. Nova Scotia-born sea captain JOSHUA SLOCUM sailed his gaff-rigged sloop Spray into the harbour as part of the first solo circumnavigation of the world, spending several months in Australia before continuing his epic voyage.

To honour this remarkable seaman, the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron will stage a special Captain Slocum Race for gaff-rigged yachts as the first in a series of four Sunday races for gaffers "with a good turn of speed, with or without spinnaker" on Sunday, October 13.
Noted artist and square-rig Cape Horner, DENNIS ADAMS, is crafting a bronze perpetual trophy for the series winner, with the Captain Slocum Race planned as an annual event.
CLIPPER CUP TO TOWNSVILLE YACHT
The Clipper Cup was the original trophy for the international ocean racing series conducted by the Royal Hawaiian Ocean Race Club, now called the Kenwood Cup.

Somehow the Clipper Cup has ended up in North Queensland as the major trophy for a series of races between Cairns and Port Douglas called the Mirage Resorts Clipper Cup. This year the regatta has attracted a fleet of about 40 yachts.
Victory was clinched off Four Mile Beach, Port Douglas, yesterday by WAYNE MILLAR's Townsville crew sailing the IAIN MURRAY-designed 41-footer, B-52.

The Port Douglas victory was the yacht's sixth straight win in the IMS division. It was not an easy win, with strong competition from the Victorian sloop Bartercard Morning Mist, skippered by ALF NEATE.

This is the second major win in recent weeks by Townsville yachts. No Fearr, a Farr-39 skippered by CAREY RAMM, won the Hayman Island Big Boat Series and followed this by taking out the International Measurement System (IMS) division of the Hamilton Island Race Week.

Both yachts are now looking further afield. B-52 is an entrant in the Gosford to Lord Howe Island race from October 26 and both she and No Fearr are expected to contest the 52nd Sydney to Hobart, starting on December 26.
AUSTRALIAN WOMEN HELP OLYMPIC BID

SUSAN WALTERS and her crew of KARYN GOJNICH and ALEX MURRAY have missed the cut in the 1996 Women's International Match Racing Championships just completed at Marblehead, Massachusetts, but they have added to a strong bid to have a women's match race event included in the Sydney 2000 Olympics.

Women sailors from Bermuda, Denmark, Germany, Canada, the U.S. and Australia contested the Massachusetts series, sailing Sonar class keelboats designed by BRUCE KIRBY, who created the Olympic Laser class.

While the Australians failed to reach the semifinals, they put on a good showing in the round-robin series, including having COURTNEY BECKER-DEY, U.S. Olympic bronze medallist in the 470 class, black-flagged in one encounter.
American HANNAH HEWITT proved too strong with a win in the final from PAULA LEWIN of Bermuda. BECKER-DEY finished third, beating another American, BETSY ALISON.

The Marblehead regatta was just one of a circuit of events that have emerged as interest grows in women's match racing, with the International Sailing Federation recommending to the International Olympic Committee that this discipline be added to the Olympic yachting in Sydney in 2000.
AUSTRALIA SKIFF IN OLYMPIC BID

Talking of Olympic classes, one new class to be introduced for Sydney 2000 will be a high-performance skiff-type dinghy with an asymmetric spinnaker, sailed by a crew of two on trapeze and open to both men and women.
Extensive trials were held early this month on Lake Garda in Italy and further trials sailed this week off Hayling Island in England.

The choice, to be made by the International Sailing Federation (ISAF) in November, appears to be between the 49er, designed by Australian FRANK BETHWAITE, and the US-designed dinghies, the 5000 and the Boss.
In the latest trials, the 49er won two races, the Boss took out one.

The 49ers will show their sailing ability on Sydney Harbour today and over the weekend as they sail in the special Olympic Test Regatta being put on for Frenchman MICHELLE BARBIER, chairman of the ISAF's Working Party for Sydney 2000.
The regatta is aimed at convincing the ISAF that Sydney Harbour is big enough and has fair winds to conduct several of the Olympic classes in 2000.

Middle Harbour Yacht Club is running races for the 49ers and also 505 dinghies on the Sound near the Heads at the weekend, while on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron, assisted by the Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club, will conduct Olympic course races for Lasers, Laser Radials, Flying 11s and 420s on areas either east or west of Bradley's Head.
VICTORIAN YACHT ON COURSE FOR SYDNEY TO HOBART

Collins Street orthodontist and immediate past commodore of the Royal Yacht Club of Victoria, BRUCE TAYLOR, has sailed his Hick-36, JLW Chutzpah, to victory in the Ocean Racing Club of Victoria (ORCV)'s Winter Series.

JLW Chutzpah won the seventh and final race of the June through September series, from Portsea to Hastings, last weekend to finish with 595 points, ahead of DAVID GOETZ's Brighton Star from the Royal Brighton Yacht Club on 587.
The race to Hastings, the only one sailed in the open waters of Bass Strait, had been postponed a week because of reports that several containers had been washed off a freighter in the course area.
It was an excellent performance by Chutzpah as she missed the sixth race on Port Phillip when TAYLOR had the 10.5 metre sloop trucked to North Queensland to compete in Hamilton Island Race Week.
TAYLOR said Race Week and the Winter Series had been an excellent preparation for his major objective -- to score an IMS victory in the Sydney to Hobart.

"The weather in the last race of the ORCV series ranged from fresh breezes to fickle conditions, similar to those in Hobart's Derwent River that have frustrated our efforts in past Sydney to Hobarts," TAYLOR said.

JLW Chutzpah, which is sponsored by JONES LANG WOOTTON, was in second place for overall handicap honours last year until she encountered light winds near Tasman Island in the final 12 hours of the race.
The Victorian Water Police got into the act when they "pulled over" Brighton Star near the finish of the race in Westernport and asked to see her registration papers.
Brighton Star, the former Sword of Orion, is registered as an Australian ship as she has sailed internationally. As such it is apparently not listed on the Victorian Water Police computers.
This sort of thing has become more common since yacht registration became compulsory.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine
